QF.id: XXVA Sales and Distribution of Research Services_22

question.text: The concept of 'pre-deal research' in the context of research services refers to:

answer.text: Research conducted before a client makes any investment decision
Research that can be published as an investor education activity which is not prohibited by the solicitation-related restrictions in Regulation 18(4)-(6)
Research conducted by interns before they become full-time analysts
Research that is only shared with the research entity's internal team

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook supports the publication of pre-deal research as an investor education activity that is not prohibited by Regulation 18(4)-(6). It sits within the carve-outs that allow certain investor education activities even where other solicitation-related activities are restricted. The Trap: Pre-deal research has a specific regulatory meaning here; it is not general pre-investment research, intern output, or internal-only material. Note: The "cooling-off period" or "blackout period" framing around investment banking transactions was not found in the checked workbook page and is intentionally avoided here.
